question: The parliamentary system of the Government in India is based on the pattern of which of the following Parliamentary Governments?
solution:
The correct answer is __**British**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The parliamentary system of government in India is largely based on the British model.
 
• India adopted the British parliamentary system as it was familiar to the Indian leaders who were exposed to British legal and parliamentary traditions.
 
• The Indian parliamentary system comprises two houses: the Lok Sabha (House of the People) and the Rajya Sabha (Council of States), similar to the British Parliament's House of Commons and House of Lords.
 
• The President of India is the constitutional head of the country, similar to the British monarch, while the Prime Minister of India is the head of government, similar to the British Prime Minister.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Parliamentary System:**

 
 
• A parliamentary system is a system of democratic governance where the executive branch derives its legitimacy from and is accountable to the legislature (parliament); the executive and legislative branches are thus interconnected.
 
• In a parliamentary system, the head of state is usually different from the head of government. The head of government is typically the prime minister, who is appointed by the head of state.
 
 
 
• **Lok Sabha:**
 
 
• The Lok Sabha, or House of the People, is the lower house of India's bicameral parliament. Its members are directly elected by the people of India.
 
• The Lok Sabha is responsible for making laws and representing the people's interests. It has significant powers, including the ability to pass money bills and hold the government accountable.
 
 
 
• **Rajya Sabha:**
 
 
• The Rajya Sabha, or Council of States, is the upper house of India's bicameral parliament. Its members are elected by the legislative assemblies of states and union territories.
 
• The Rajya Sabha represents the states and union territories and acts as a revising chamber for legislation passed by the Lok Sabha.
 
 
 
• **Prime Minister:**
 
 
• The Prime Minister of India is the head of government and is appointed by the President. The Prime Minister is usually the leader of the majority party or coalition in the Lok Sabha.
 
• The Prime Minister leads the executive branch of the government, sets government policy, and represents the country in international affairs.
 
 
 
• **President:**
 
 
• The President of India is the head of state and is elected by an electoral college consisting of the members of both houses of parliament and the legislative assemblies of states and union territories.
 
• The President has a range of powers and functions, including appointing the Prime Minister, representing the country in ceremonial matters, and acting as the supreme commander of the armed forces.
